email_sequences.subject: Stories that spark conversations — Bob Mills x Hope Fellowship
email_sequences.body:
Hi Angela,

It was wonderful meeting you at BookExpo 2026! Thank you for stopping by my booth and sharing about Hope Fellowship's youth ministry and summer reading program.

You mentioned you were looking for titles that could engage your youth group — books that don't just entertain but give your students something meaningful to talk about. That's exactly why I write.

I believe the best science fiction does more than imagine the future. It asks the questions that matter:

— What does it take to build a community when everything around you is hostile?
— How do you lead with courage when the odds are stacked against you?
— What do you hold onto when the familiar is gone?

Those aren't just space-exploration questions. They're the questions every young person is wrestling with — identity, purpose, belonging, courage. My books put those questions into stories your students will love.

Here's what might work well for a youth group setting:

🚀 NO BLUE SKY (5 vols) — Mars Colonization
Characters building a new society from scratch. Themes: community, sacrifice, leadership.

🌙 LUNAR FOUNDATION (4 vols) — Moon Base Survival
Survival, teamwork, and what it means to be your brother's keeper.

🪐 AGE OF LIGHTSHIPS (4 vols) — Solar System Adventure
Exploration, discovery, and navigating the unknown with faith and grit.

You mentioned the title breakdown was TBD — I'd love to help you figure out what fits best. Reply to this email and I'll send you:

✅ A free PDF sampler with the first chapters of each series
✅ A list of discussion-worthy themes per book, perfect for youth group talks
✅ Bulk pricing options for ministry/group purchases

Blessings,
Bob Mills

P.S. If you'd like, I can also put together short discussion questions for any book you choose — free of charge. I love knowing my stories are being used to spark real conversations.

email_sequences.subject: Why science fiction and youth ministry are a perfect match, Angela
email_sequences.body:
Hi Angela,

I wanted to share a little more about why I think science fiction — and my books in particular — can be such a powerful tool for youth ministry.

When I speak with youth leaders, they tell me the biggest challenge is getting students to engage with big ideas in a way that feels relevant, not preachy. They want conversations that go deeper than "what did you do this weekend?" but don't feel like a sermon.

Science fiction does something unique. It creates a safe distance — it's not about "us," it's about people on Mars or the Moon — and yet every conflict, every moral choice, every act of courage or failure hits right at home. Students can wrestle with questions of right and wrong, sacrifice and selfishness, hope and despair — without feeling like they're being taught a lesson.

Here are just a few themes from my series that map naturally to faith-based discussion:

📕 Built from Dust (No Blue Sky #1)
— Starting something new from nothing. What does it take to build a community of faith?
— Sacrifice for the greater good. When is it worth giving up something you want for others?

🌙 Moon Rock (Lunar Foundation #1)
— Survival and trust. Who do you rely on when everything falls apart?
— Forgiveness in close quarters. How do you rebuild relationships after failure?

🚀 Sunward Exodus (Age of Lightships #1)
— Stepping into the unknown. What does courage look like when you're afraid?
— Leadership and service. What makes a good leader?

🎁 I'd love to send you a free youth group discussion guide for any book that interests you. Just reply with the title — no purchase necessary. I want these books to serve your ministry.

In fellowship,
Bob Mills
